name: Prologis
description: Prologis is the largest owner of logistics warehouses in the world. It leases modern distribution buildings to more than 4,000 customers in its consolidated portfolio (649 million sq ft) and, counting buildings held in funds it manages, about 6,500 customers across 1.3 billion sq ft. Nearly all money is rent: multi-year leases with contractual rent bumps plus reimbursement of most property operating costs, with growth from rolling old leases up to current market rents and from building new warehouses. A smaller second business earns management fees and occasional performance fees (promotes) from co-investment funds Prologis runs with outside investors ($62.4B gross book value, 562 million sq ft in ten unconsolidated ventures at Dec 31, 2025). Prologis is also starting to develop data centers, with power procurement. Southern California is the only market at 10 percent or more of revenue.

businessLines.how: Tenants pay monthly rent under multi-year leases (weighted average remaining term in the filing: 70 months) plus reimbursement of most property taxes and operating costs; growth comes from contractual rent bumps, marking expiring leases to higher market rent, and completing new buildings.
businessLines.description: Ownership and leasing of logistics buildings, development of new ones, land, and other real estate including renewable energy assets. The 10-K says rental operations alone generate 90 to 95 percent of consolidated revenue.

businessLines.description: Management of properties held by ten unconsolidated co-investment ventures, plus leasing, development, financing and disposition services.
